text: 富贵不能淫，贫贱不能移，威武不能屈
pinyin: fù guì bù néng yín, pín jiàn bù néng yí, wēi wǔ bù néng qū
literal: wealth · rank · cannot · corrupt, poverty · lowliness · cannot · shift, power · force · cannot · bend
natural: unmoved by wealth, poverty or force

meaning.en: Neither riches, poverty nor threats can sway a person of true integrity.
meaning.zh: 金钱地位不能使他迷惑，贫穷低微不能使他改变操守，权势武力不能使他屈服。形容坚定不移的大丈夫气概。

equivalents: unbending in the face of temptation and threat

examples.zh: 他富贵不能淫，贫贱不能移，威武不能屈，是真正的大丈夫。
examples.en: Riches could not corrupt him, poverty could not shift him, force could not bend him; he was a true man of integrity.

examples.zh: 面对诱惑，他做到了富贵不能淫。
examples.en: Faced with temptation, he proved that wealth could not corrupt him.

examples.zh: 威武不能屈，这是革命者的气节。
examples.en: Not bowing to force is the integrity of a revolutionary.

story.en: Mencius defines the 'great man' (大丈夫) as one whom 'wealth and rank cannot corrupt, poverty cannot shift, and force cannot bend' (富贵不能淫，贫贱不能移，威武不能屈).
story.zh: 《孟子·滕文公下》：“居天下之广居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道……富贵不能淫，贫贱不能移，威武不能屈，此之谓大丈夫。”

usage.en: Praise of moral integrity; formal, often quoted whole or in part.
usage.zh: 称赞高尚气节，书面语，可全引也可只引一部分。

pinyin: bīng mǎ wèi dòng, liáng cǎo xiān xíng
literal: troops · horses · not yet · move, grain · fodder · first · go

meaning.en: Before the army moves, its supplies must go ahead: prepare thoroughly before acting.
meaning.zh: 军队出发之前，粮食草料要先运送。比喻行动之前先做好物质准备。

examples.zh: 兵马未动，粮草先行，出远门之前先把行李准备好。
examples.en: Provisions go before the troops; before a long trip, get your luggage ready.

examples.zh: 兵马未动，项目要先落实资金。
examples.en: Before the troops move, the project must secure its funding.

examples.zh: 粮草先行，后勤工作最要紧。
examples.en: Supplies go first; logistics matters most.

usage.en: Used about preparation; light, metaphorical.
usage.zh: 用于强调事先准备，有比喻色彩。

pinyin: xiá lù xiāng féng yǒng zhě shèng
literal: narrow · road · meet · brave · one · wins
natural: in a head-on clash the bold win

meaning.en: When two forces meet on a narrow path, the braver one wins.
meaning.zh: 双方在狭窄的路上相遇，勇敢的一方取胜。比喻对手相当时，勇敢果断者获胜。

equivalents: when push comes to shove, the bold prevail

examples.zh: 决赛是狭路相逢勇者胜，哪一队更敢拼就赢。
examples.en: The final is a clash on a narrow road, and the bolder team will win.

examples.zh: 狭路相逢勇者胜，我们要有必胜的信心。
examples.en: When we meet head-on, the brave win; we must be confident of victory.

examples.zh: 谈判桌上狭路相逢勇者胜。
examples.en: At the negotiating table, when equals meet, the bold prevail.

usage.en: Often a pep-talk before contests.
usage.zh: 常用于比赛前鼓劲。

pinyin: shēn zhèng bù pà yǐng zi xié
literal: body · upright · not · fear · shadow · slanted
natural: an upright person has nothing to fear from gossip

meaning.en: If you stand straight, you need not fear a crooked shadow: those who act rightly fear no slander.
meaning.zh: 自己行为端正，就不怕别人说闲话。

equivalents: an honest man has nothing to hide
a clear conscience fears no accusation

examples.zh: 身正不怕影子斜，随便他们怎么说。
examples.en: An upright body fears no crooked shadow; let them say what they like.

examples.zh: 他相信身正不怕影子斜，从不解释。
examples.en: He believes that those who stand straight need not fear a crooked shadow, and never explains himself.

examples.zh: 身正不怕影子斜，我愿意接受检查。
examples.en: I've nothing to hide, and I welcome inspection.

usage.en: Self-defence against rumours; casual.
usage.zh: 用来回应流言，口语。

pinyin: rén fēi shèng xián, shú néng wú guò
literal: person · not · sage · worthy, who · can · lack · fault

meaning.en: Nobody is a saint, so who can be free from mistakes?
meaning.zh: 人不是圣人，谁能没有过错呢？表示人人都会犯错，应该宽容。

examples.zh: 人非圣贤，孰能无过，改了就好。
examples.en: Nobody is perfect; mistakes are fine as long as you correct them.

examples.zh: 人非圣贤孰能无过，请原谅他这一次。
examples.en: To err is human; please forgive him this once.

examples.zh: 人非圣贤，孰能无过，别太自责。
examples.en: We're not saints and can't be free of faults, so don't blame yourself too much.

usage.en: Used to forgive or console; formal-ish.
usage.zh: 用来宽慰或求情，略带书面色彩。

pinyin: yī rén dé dào, jī quǎn shēng tiān
literal: one · person · attain · Dao, chickens · dogs · ascend · heaven
natural: when one rises, all his hangers-on rise too

meaning.en: When one person attains power, even his chickens and dogs rise to heaven: all his associates profit.
meaning.zh: 一个人得势，他身边的人也跟着沾光。

equivalents: when one man rises, his whole clan rises with him

examples.zh: 他一当上局长，亲戚朋友都得了好处，真是一人得道，鸡犬升天。
examples.en: Once he became bureau chief, all his relatives and friends benefited: truly when one man attains the Way, even his chickens and dogs ascend.

examples.zh: 别以为一人得道，鸡犬升天，大家要靠实力。
examples.en: Don't expect your whole circle to rise with you; people must rely on ability.

examples.zh: 这种一人得道的风气要不得。
examples.en: This habit of everyone around the boss profiting is unacceptable.

story.en: A legend of Liu An, Prince of Huainan, who was said to ascend to heaven after attaining the Way, with his household animals also becoming immortal: 'his dogs barked in the sky and his chickens crowed among the clouds'.
story.zh: 汉代传说：淮南王刘安得道成仙，全家升天，连家中鸡犬也跟着成仙。《论衡·道虚》载：“犬吠于天上，鸡鸣于云中。”

usage.en: Derogatory, about cronyism and nepotism.
usage.zh: 贬义，讽刺裙带关系。

pinyin: yù jiā zhī zuì, hé huàn wú cí
literal: wish · to impose · its · crime, why · worry · lack · pretext
natural: if they want to condemn you, they'll find a pretext

meaning.en: If someone wants to charge you with a crime, they will always find an excuse.
meaning.zh: 想要给人加上罪名，还怕找不到借口吗？形容蓄意陷害。

equivalents: give a dog a bad name and hang him

examples.zh: 欲加之罪，何患无辞，他们根本不想听我解释。
examples.en: If they want to blame me they'll find an excuse; they don't want to hear my explanation.

examples.zh: 这明明是欲加之罪，我不服。
examples.en: This is clearly a trumped-up charge, and I don't accept it.

examples.zh: 历史上不少冤案都是欲加之罪。
examples.en: Many a wrongful case in history was a fabricated charge.

story.en: In the Zuo Commentary, when Duke Hui of Jin forced Li Ke to die, Li Ke replied: 'If you wish to impose a charge, can you lack words?' (欲加之罪，其无辞乎). The modern form is 何患无辞.
story.zh: 《左传·僖公十年》：晋惠公逼里克自杀，里克说：“欲加之罪，其无辞乎？”后世常作“欲加之罪，何患无辞”。

usage.en: About unjust accusations; formal.
usage.zh: 指蓄意诬陷，书面语。

pinyin: shuǐ néng zài zhōu, yì néng fù zhōu
literal: water · can · carry · boat, also · can · capsize · boat
natural: the people can support or topple a ruler

meaning.en: Water can carry a boat, and also capsize it: the people can sustain a ruler or overthrow him.
meaning.zh: 水可以承载船，也可以掀翻船。比喻民众既能拥戴君主，也能推翻君主。

equivalents: the people can make or break a ruler
what lifts you up can bring you down

examples.zh: 水能载舟，亦能覆舟，民意不可忽视。
examples.en: Water can carry the boat and also overturn it; public opinion cannot be ignored.

examples.zh: 互联网上的舆论水能载舟，也能覆舟。
examples.en: Online opinion is like water that can carry or capsize the boat.

examples.zh: 水能载舟，君王要懂得敬畏人民。
examples.en: The ruler must learn to respect the people.

story.en: Xunzi: 'The ruler is the boat and the common people are the water; water carries the boat and water capsizes the boat' (君者舟也，庶人者水也；水则载舟，水则覆舟).
story.zh: 《荀子·王制》：“君者，舟也；庶人者，水也。水则载舟，水则覆舟。”

usage.en: Common in political commentary and about public opinion.
usage.zh: 常用于政治评论和谈论民意。

text: 穷则独善其身，达则兼济天下
pinyin: qióng zé dú shàn qí shēn, dá zé jiān jì tiān xià
literal: poor · then · alone · perfect · one's · self, successful · then · together · help · world
natural: cultivate yourself in adversity, serve all in success

meaning.en: In adversity, cultivate oneself; when successful, benefit the whole world.
meaning.zh: 不得志时就修养自己的品德，得志时就让天下人都得到好处。

equivalents: improve yourself in hard times, help others in good times

examples.zh: 穷则独善其身，达则兼济天下，这是古代士人的理想。
examples.en: In hardship, perfect oneself; when successful, benefit all: this was the ideal of the ancient scholar.

examples.zh: 他有钱以后捐款办学，真是达则兼济天下。
examples.en: Once rich he donated to build schools, truly helping the world when successful.

examples.zh: 兼济天下是读书人的抱负。
examples.en: Benefiting the world is a scholar's ambition.

story.en: Mencius: 'When poor, perfect oneself alone; when successful, help the whole world together' (穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下).
story.zh: 《孟子·尽心上》：“古之人，得志，泽加于民；不得志，修身见于世。穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下。”

usage.en: Describes a gentleman's attitude to fortune; formal.
usage.zh: 说明君子的处世原则，书面语。

pinyin: qián bù zháo cūn, hòu bù zháo diàn
literal: front · not · reach · village, behind · not · reach · inn

meaning.en: No village ahead and no inn behind: stranded in a remote place with nowhere to turn.
meaning.zh: 前面没有村庄，后面没有旅店。形容处在荒僻的地方，无处投宿，也比喻进退两难。

examples.zh: 车坏在前不着村，后不着店的地方，真让人着急。
examples.en: The car broke down in the middle of nowhere, which was worrying.

examples.zh: 这里前不着村后不着店，咱们得赶紧找地方过夜。
examples.en: There's neither village nor inn nearby; we must find a place for the night.

examples.zh: 他陷入前不着村，后不着店的境地。
examples.en: He found himself with neither village ahead nor inn behind.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; casual.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或定语，口语。

text: 三十年河东，三十年河西
pinyin: sān shí nián hé dōng, sān shí nián hé xī
literal: thirty · years · river · east, thirty · years · river · west

meaning.en: For thirty years the river runs on the east side, then thirty on the west: fortunes change.
meaning.zh: 黄河改道，三十年河东，三十年河西。比喻盛衰变化无常，兴衰轮流转。

examples.zh: 三十年河东，三十年河西，别看不起穷人。
examples.en: The river's course shifts every thirty years; don't look down on the poor.

examples.zh: 谁知三十年河东，他如今成了大老板。
examples.en: Who knew fortunes would turn: he's now a big boss.

examples.zh: 三十年河东，山水轮流转，一时的得失不必在意。
examples.en: The river changes sides; don't mind temporary gains and losses.

usage.en: A consolation or warning about reversals of fortune; often 莫欺少年穷.
usage.zh: 宽慰或警告世事变迁，常与“莫欺少年穷”连用。

pinyin: yǎng bīng qiān rì, yòng bīng yī shí
literal: raise · soldiers · thousand · days, use · soldiers · one · moment

meaning.en: Troops are trained for a thousand days to be used in a single moment: preparation pays off at the critical time.
meaning.zh: 平时长期供养训练军队，是为了关键时刻使用。比喻平时的准备是为了关键时刻。

equivalents: train for years, perform for a day
be ready when the moment comes

examples.zh: 养兵千日，用兵一时，现在是考验队伍的时候了。
examples.en: A thousand days of training for one moment of use: now is the time to test the team.

examples.zh: 养兵千日，关键时刻你可要顶上去。
examples.en: After a thousand days of upkeep, you must step up now.

examples.zh: 养兵千日用兵一时，平时的训练就是为了今天。
examples.en: Training in ordinary times was for today.

usage.en: Often said when asking a trained person to deliver.
usage.zh: 常用来要求平时受培养的人在关键时刻出力。

text: 路遥知马力，日久见人心
pinyin: lù yáo zhī mǎ lì, rì jiǔ jiàn rén xīn
literal: road · far · know · horse · strength, days · long · see · person · heart

meaning.en: A long road tests a horse's strength and time reveals a person's heart.
meaning.zh: 路途遥远才能知道马的力气，时间长了才能看出人心的好坏。

equivalents: a friend in need is a friend indeed

examples.zh: 路遥知马力，日久见人心，他是个可靠的朋友。
examples.en: A long road shows a horse's strength and time shows a person's heart; he's a reliable friend.

examples.zh: 路遥知马力，相处久了你就明白了。
examples.en: The road shows the horse; after a while you'll understand.

examples.zh: 路遥知马力，日久见人心，别急着下结论。
examples.en: Time shows who people really are, so don't rush to a conclusion.

usage.en: About judging someone's character over time.
usage.zh: 谈论要长期考察人的品质。

pinyin: bīng lái jiàng dǎng, shuǐ lái tǔ yǎn
literal: troops · come · general · block, water · come · earth · dam
natural: deal with each problem as it comes

meaning.en: When troops come, generals hold them off; when floods come, earth dams them: deal with each trouble as it arises.
meaning.zh: 敌人来了有将领抵挡，洪水来了用土掩埋。比喻随机应变，遇到什么问题就用相应办法对付。

equivalents: we'll cross that bridge when we come to it

examples.zh: 别担心，兵来将挡，水来土掩，到时候再说。
examples.en: Don't worry; we'll deal with whatever comes when it comes.

examples.zh: 兵来将挡，水来土掩，我们早有应对方案。
examples.en: Whatever comes, we'll handle it; we already have a plan.

examples.zh: 做生意要兵来将挡，随机应变。
examples.en: In business you must handle each threat as it comes.

usage.en: Casual attitude; can sound carefree.
usage.zh: 口语，表示随机应变，有时显得无所谓。

text: 纸上得来终觉浅，绝知此事要躬行
pinyin: zhǐ shàng dé lái zhōng jué qiǎn, jué zhī cǐ shì yào gōng xíng
literal: paper · on · obtain · ultimately · feel · shallow, utterly · know · this · matter · must · practise · in person
natural: practice is the only true knowledge

meaning.en: Knowledge from books is always shallow; to truly understand, you must practise it yourself.
meaning.zh: 从书本上得来的知识终究是浅薄的，要想透彻了解，必须亲身实践。

equivalents: theory is not enough; you must do it yourself

examples.zh: 纸上得来终觉浅，绝知此事要躬行，学游泳必须下水。
examples.en: Book knowledge is always shallow; to truly know, practise it: you must get in the water to learn to swim.

examples.zh: 纸上得来终觉浅，他决定去实地考察。
examples.en: Learning from paper is shallow, so he decided to investigate on the spot.

examples.zh: 光看书不够，纸上得来终觉浅。
examples.en: Reading is not enough: what comes from paper is shallow.

story.en: Lu You's poem to his son Ziyu: 'What is learned from paper is always shallow; to truly know a thing you must do it yourself' (纸上得来终觉浅，绝知此事要躬行).
story.zh: 陆游《冬夜读书示子聿》：“古人学问无遗力，少壮工夫老始成。纸上得来终觉浅，绝知此事要躬行。”

usage.en: Encouragement to practise; poetic, often quoted in education.
usage.zh: 鼓励实践，诗句，教育场合常引。

pinyin: nán dēng dà yǎ zhī táng
literal: hard · ascend · great · elegance · 's · hall

meaning.en: Too crude or lowbrow to be presented in refined settings.
meaning.zh: 不够高雅精致，不能在正式、高雅的场合出现。

examples.zh: 这种小调难登大雅之堂，但民间很受欢迎。
examples.en: This kind of ditty is hardly fit for formal settings, but it's very popular among ordinary people.

examples.zh: 他的作品被批评为难登大雅之堂。
examples.en: His work was criticised as unfit for polite society.

examples.zh: 路边小吃虽然难登大雅之堂，却很美味。
examples.en: Street snacks may not be fit for a formal banquet, but they're delicious.

usage.en: Often with 虽然…但…; sometimes self-deprecating.
usage.zh: 常与“虽然……但……”连用，有时是自谦。

pinyin: shì kě rěn, shú bù kě rěn
literal: this · can · be tolerated, what · not · can · be tolerated
natural: if this can be borne, what cannot?

meaning.en: If this can be tolerated, then nothing can't: it's utterly intolerable.
meaning.zh: 如果这件事都可以容忍，还有什么不能容忍的呢？表示极其愤慨，无法容忍。

examples.zh: 这种欺人太甚的行为，是可忍，孰不可忍！
examples.en: Such bullying is beyond the pale; if this can be borne, what cannot?

examples.zh: 是可忍孰不可忍，我们必须表明立场。
examples.en: This is intolerable and we must make our stance clear.

examples.zh: 对这种不公正，是可忍，孰不可忍？
examples.en: If this injustice can be tolerated, what can't?

story.en: Confucius, on the Ji family using eight rows of dancers reserved for the king: 'If this can be tolerated, what cannot be tolerated?' (是可忍也，孰不可忍也).
story.zh: 《论语·八佾》：“孔子谓季氏：八佾舞于庭，是可忍也，孰不可忍也！”

usage.en: Expression of outrage; formal, often a rhetorical question.
usage.zh: 表示愤怒，书面语，多作反问。

text: 鸡犬之声相闻，民至老死不相往来
pinyin: jī quǎn zhī shēng xiāng wén, mín zhì lǎo sǐ bù xiāng wǎng lái
literal: chickens · dogs · 's · sounds · mutually · heard, people · until · old · death · not · mutually · visit

meaning.en: Neighbouring villages can hear each other's cocks and dogs, yet people live and die without ever visiting: Laozi's picture of a simple, self-contained society.
meaning.zh: 邻国之间互相能听见鸡鸣狗叫，百姓到老死也不互相往来。是老子描绘的理想的小国寡民社会。

examples.zh: 老子描绘的“鸡犬之声相闻，民至老死不相往来”是一种理想社会。
examples.en: Laozi's picture of villages close enough to hear each other's dogs and hens yet who never visit was an ideal society.

examples.zh: 鸡犬之声相闻，邻居却从不来往，这就是现代城市的写照。
examples.en: Close enough to hear each other's dogs and hens yet never speaking: this is modern city life.

examples.zh: 鸡犬之声相闻的小村庄，宁静而偏僻。
examples.en: A small village within earshot of its neighbours' hens and dogs, quiet and remote.

story.en: Laozi ch. 80 describes a small state where 'neighbouring states look across to each other, the sounds of chickens and dogs are heard, yet the people grow old and die without visiting' (邻国相望，鸡犬之声相闻，民至老死，不相往来).
story.zh: 《老子》第八十章：“邻国相望，鸡犬之声相闻，民至老死，不相往来。”

usage.en: Often cited for villages' peace or for modern neighbourly indifference.
usage.zh: 可形容乡村宁静，也可讽刺现代邻里疏远。

pinyin: liú shuǐ bù fǔ, hù shū bù dù
literal: flowing · water · not · rot, door · pivot · not · worm-eaten

meaning.en: Running water does not stagnate and a door pivot is not eaten by worms: constant movement prevents decay.
meaning.zh: 流动的水不会腐臭，经常转动的门轴不会被虫蛀。比喻经常运动、更新的事物不易受到侵蚀。

equivalents: a rolling stone gathers no moss (in the positive sense)

examples.zh: 流水不腐，户枢不蠹，坚持运动才能保持健康。
examples.en: Running water doesn't go stale and a busy hinge doesn't rot; keep exercising to stay healthy.

examples.zh: 流水不腐，企业要不断创新。
examples.en: Running water doesn't rot, so a company must keep innovating.

examples.zh: 流水不腐，爷爷每天散步从不间断。
examples.en: Running water never goes bad, and Grandad walks every day without fail.

story.en: Lüshi Chunqiu: 'Flowing water does not rot, and a door pivot is not worm-eaten, because they move' (流水不腐，户枢不蝼，动也).
story.zh: 《吕氏春秋·尽数》：“流水不腐，户枢不蝼，动也。形气亦然。形不动则精不流，精不流则气郁。”

usage.en: Common in health, management and education talk.
usage.zh: 常用于养生、管理、教育等话题。

pinyin: qǔ zhī bù jìn, yòng zhī bù jié
literal: take · it · not · exhausted, use · it · not · run dry

meaning.en: Never exhausted however much is taken or used.
meaning.zh: 怎么取也取不完，怎么用也用不光。形容资源极其丰富。

examples.zh: 太阳能是取之不尽，用之不竭的清洁能源。
examples.en: Solar power is an inexhaustible clean energy source.

examples.zh: 别以为资源取之不尽用之不竭。
examples.en: Don't assume resources are endless.

examples.zh: 他有取之不尽的创作灵感。
examples.en: He has an inexhaustible supply of creative inspiration.

story.en: Su Shi's 'Red Cliff Rhapsody' says of the breeze and moon: 'No one forbids taking them, and using them never runs dry' (取之无禁，用之不竭). The idiom reshapes the line.
story.zh: 苏轼《赤壁赋》：“惟江上之清风，与山间之明月……取之无禁，用之不竭。”成语由此演变。

usage.en: Attributive or predicate; typically about resources, ideas.
usage.zh: 作定语或谓语，常形容资源、灵感等。

pinyin: yī chuán shí, shí chuán bǎi
literal: one · pass on · ten, ten · pass on · hundred

meaning.en: One person tells ten, ten tell a hundred: news spreads quickly by word of mouth.
meaning.zh: 一个人传给十个人，十个人传给一百个人。形容消息传播很快。

examples.zh: 一传十，十传百，不久全村人都知道了。
examples.en: One told ten and ten told a hundred; soon the whole village knew.

examples.zh: 好口碑一传十十传百，生意越来越好。
examples.en: A good reputation spreads by word of mouth and business keeps getting better.

examples.zh: 这个传闻一传十，十传百，越传越离谱。
examples.en: The rumour spread from one to ten to a hundred, getting wilder each time.

usage.en: Used for news, rumours and reputation; casual.
usage.zh: 形容消息、传闻、口碑扩散，口语。

pinyin: méi yǒu guī jǔ, bù chéng fāng yuán
literal: without · compass · square, not · form · square · round

meaning.en: Without compass and set-square you cannot draw squares and circles: without rules, nothing is in order.
meaning.zh: 没有圆规和曲尺，就画不出方形和圆形。比喻做事必须有规则和标准。

equivalents: without rules there is no order

examples.zh: 没有规矩，不成方圆，公司必须有明确的制度。
examples.en: Without compass and square, no circles and squares; a company needs clear rules.

examples.zh: 没有规矩不成方圆，孩子从小就要懂规矩。
examples.en: Without rules there's no order; children should learn rules young.

examples.zh: 不以规矩，不能成方圆，这是千古名言。
examples.en: 'Without compass and square you cannot form squares or circles' is a timeless saying.

story.en: Mencius: 'Without compass and carpenter's square one cannot form squares and circles' (不以规矩，不能成方圆), as a reminder that rules are essential even for sages.
story.zh: 《孟子·离娄上》：“离娄之明，公输子之巧，不以规矩，不能成方圆。”

usage.en: Advocating rules and discipline.
usage.zh: 强调规则和纪律。

pinyin: nán ér yǒu lèi bù qīng tán
literal: man · have · tears · not · lightly · flick

meaning.en: A man has tears but does not shed them lightly.
meaning.zh: 男子汉有眼泪也不轻易流下，表示坚强，只在伤心到极点时才哭。

equivalents: a real man keeps his tears in check

examples.zh: 男儿有泪不轻弹，只是未到伤心处。
examples.en: A man has tears but doesn't shed them lightly; it's just that he hasn't reached the point of grief.

examples.zh: 他从小被教育男儿有泪不轻弹。
examples.en: He was brought up to believe men don't weep easily.

examples.zh: 男儿有泪不轻弹，今天他终于哭了。
examples.en: Men don't cry easily, but today he finally wept.

usage.en: Often followed by 只是未到伤心处; some now see it as a stereotype.
usage.zh: 常接“只是未到伤心处”；现代人有时认为带有性别刻板印象。

pinyin: zǎo zhī jīn rì, hé bì dāng chū
literal: early · know · today, why · must · back then

meaning.en: If I had known this would happen, why did I act as I did then?
meaning.zh: 早知道会有今天这样的结果，当初就不该那样做。表示后悔。

equivalents: why did you do it in the first place?

examples.zh: 早知今日，何必当初，现在后悔已经晚了。
examples.en: If you'd known this would happen, why do it back then? It's too late to regret.

examples.zh: 早知今日，当初就好好学习了。
examples.en: If I'd known, I would have studied hard back then.

examples.zh: 他失败后叹道：早知今日，何必当初！
examples.en: After failing, he sighed: 'Why did I ever do it?'

usage.en: Regret or reproach; casual.
usage.zh: 表示后悔或责备，口语。

text: 只许州官放火，不许百姓点灯
pinyin: zhǐ xǔ zhōu guān fàng huǒ, bù xǔ bǎi xìng diǎn dēng
literal: only · allow · prefect · set · fire, not · allow · common · people · light · lamps
natural: one rule for me, another for you

meaning.en: Officials may set fires but commoners may not light lamps: the powerful may do as they please while ordinary people are restricted.
meaning.zh: 官员可以放火，百姓却连点灯都不允许。比喻有权势的人为所欲为，普通人却处处受限制。

equivalents: one rule for them and another for us
do as I say, not as I do

examples.zh: 只许州官放火，不许百姓点灯，这样的规定太不公平了。
examples.en: 'Officials may set fires but commoners may not light lamps': such rules are blatantly unfair.

examples.zh: 别搞只许州官放火的双重标准。
examples.en: Don't operate a double standard where officials may do anything.

examples.zh: 他自己迟到，却不许别人迟到，真是州官放火。
examples.en: He's late himself but won't let others be: the official sets fires and forbids lamps.

story.en: Lu You's notes tell of Prefect Tian Deng, who forbade the use of his taboo name 'deng' (灯/登) so that at the Lantern Festival the notice read 'This prefecture permits setting fires (放火) for three days', a tale that gave rise to the saying.
story.zh: 陆游《老学庵笔记》载：州官田登讳“灯”字，元宵节官吏贴告示称“本州照例放火三日”，后人由此概括出这句话。

usage.en: Criticism of double standards.
usage.zh: 批评双重标准。
